A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CaPo and provide readable main text, figures, tables, mathematical expressions, and Appendices A–C. Relocated results and unchanged appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original TDW-MAT and C-WAH experiments, component and agent-count ablations, qualitative analyses, and three random-seed runs.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds heterogeneous-team, RoCoBench, human-collaboration, discussion-budget, and communication-cost results.

M1.justification: The standard two-phase framework and Appendix C prompts remain unchanged. However, v2 introduces a heterogeneous-team adaptation in which CaPo independently creates and updates the meta-plan without multi-round discussion with its partner (Section 5.1 and Appendix A.2), changing the procedure for this setting.

E1.justification: v2 retains TDW-MAT and C-WAH and adds RoCoBench's Sweep Floor, Pack Grocery, and Move Rope tasks (Appendix A.4). It also introduces C-WAH collaboration with real human teammates (Appendix A.7), substantially broadening task and participant coverage.

E2.justification: ProAgent and RoCo disappear from the GPT-3.5 and LLAMA-2 TDW-MAT comparisons, but join the GPT-4 oracle comparison that previously contained RHP and CoELA (v1 Tables 1 and 5; v2 Table 1). New heterogeneous comparisons also include RHP+CoELA and MHP+CoELA (v2 Tables 5 and 2).

E3.justification: Tables 1–2 replace CoELA-relative improvement annotations with cooperation Efficiency Improvement. New protocols include RoCoBench success/step metrics, heterogeneous teams, three-person seven-point human ratings, and discussion budgets from one to five rounds. The stated sampling setting changes from top-p with p=1 to top-1; this documents a setting revision without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing component and agent-count ablations are retained. v2 adds a controlled discussion-budget study measuring failed cases and transport rates (Table 8), plus communication-cost analysis covering update frequency, message size, frames, and elapsed time (Table 9). These directly investigate previously unmeasured cost and performance tradeoffs.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 and Table 6 retain exactly the same three random-seed runs and mean/variance reporting. New tables attach variability values to additional results, but specify no new estimator, repeated-run policy, confidence interval, or significance test; their ± quantities remain undefined.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added: GPT-4 non-oracle transport rates of 74% for CaPo versus 71% for CoELA, RoCoBench Pack Grocery success rates of 0.63 versus RoCo's 0.44, and human-collaboration steps of 44±1 versus CoELA's 47±2. Heterogeneous-team, budget, and cost results are also new. The GPT-4 oracle values of 89% versus 85% already appeared in v1 Table 5 and are relocated, while several weaker-LLM comparator entries disappear.

T1.justification: Section 5 newly defines cooperation Efficiency Improvement as ΔM/M0, with M0 the larger compared metric value, introducing the normalization used in the revised tables. The DEC-POMDP formulation remains unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: cooperative meta-plan generation followed by progress-adaptive execution improves task completion and cooperation efficiency. The introduction's 16.7% GPT-3.5 and 4.7% GPT-4 improvement claims already appear in v1; additional experiments mainly broaden supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for independent meta-plans helping heterogeneous teams, bounded discussions balancing consensus and cost, and participation in planning improving human trust and communication. Section 6 also newly acknowledges that the predefined communication protocol can restrict flexibility in dynamic or heterogeneous environments; dependence on LLM capability was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v2's abstract announces code release and supplies a repository address, whereas v1 only promises release; v2's implementation paragraph still retains that future-tense promise. v2 also identifies quoted CoELA baseline results and supplies timing and communication measurements. Appendix B's environment instructions and Appendix C's prompt templates are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a CoELA framework overview and explicitly attributes foundational modules to CoELA. Appendix A.1 explains the exclusion of alternative environments, supported by added ALFRED and planning-agent references; MindAgent is removed. The central positioning around long-term cooperative planning remains intact.

P1.justification: Parts of the introduction and conclusion are rewritten, and module exposition is reorganized between Sections 3 and 4.1. The standalone reproducibility statement is removed, acknowledgments are added, and Appendix A gains subsections. The main section sequence and most method and prompt prose remain stable.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 are substantially reorganized with GPT-4 and heterogeneous-team columns, revised annotations, and result-source markers. v1 Table 5's GPT-4 results move into Table 1; v2 introduces a heterogeneous Table 5 and four additional experimental tables. Most figures and prompt panels are retained, with limited resizing and reflow.

improvement.justification: The new discussion-budget and communication-cost studies directly strengthen support for CaPo's efficiency design, while heterogeneous-team and RoCoBench experiments broaden validation. Clearer CoELA attribution also improves transparency. These gains are limited by underdescribed new protocols, undefined ± statistics, only three human participants, and the removal of GPT-3.5/LLAMA-2 ProAgent and RoCo comparisons.
